agree.reason: This reader is happy saving about $25 a visit and has no complaint, so the email gives them little reason to switch back: the $99 offer might get one trial booking, but it never says what regular visits will cost after that or that they can cancel any time.

honest.reason: Every figure is accurate and the email rightly avoids promising the same cleaner every time, but the subject line 'We've fixed it' claims more than the body does, since the price problem isn't fixed.

works_the_facts.reason: The strongest numbers are missing: only 1 of 18 cleaners has left since July, compared with 7 of 18 last year; $99 is $41 less than the app's $140; and the regular price gap is $25 a visit.

right_comparison.reason: It fairly says the app services mostly use contractors with no insurance on the visit, but it gives neither side's actual price ($165 against $140), which is the comparison this reader is making.

qualification.reason: The offer has a checkable end date (December 31), and the backup cleaner covers sick days and holidays, so the claim about regular cleaners is honestly qualified; it gives no evidence (like the turnover figure) that the regular-cleaner system is holding up.

objections.reason: Pointing to employees and insurance only partly answers 'why pay $25 more?', and the email leaves out the no-contract, cancel-anytime commitment that would make trying it again feel low-risk.

fit.reason: It's a plain, roughly 150-word email with a clear call to action, and it properly drops the 'same cleaner every time' promise the owner said she couldn't keep.
